solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: This could be apt thing done by Ginger Rogers?

blocks.note: surface reading: something that might well be fitting or suitable
setter's reading: the letters of this word set in motion, jigging about into a new order, which is what the answer literally describes

explanation.surface: A tribute to the famous dancing partner of Fred Astaire and her suitably nimble footwork.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the answer as a description: TAP is APT 'dancing', its letters rearranged. Ginger Rogers was a Hollywood star famous for dance routines with Fred Astaire.
explanation.definitionFit: Rogers performed rhythmic routines in metal-plated shoes on film, so this kind of footwork is something she did.

clue.text: Trump put on small crowns

indicators.note: in a down clue, one thing put on another sits on top, so the first part comes before the second

blocks.note: to trump something is to top it, to outdo it
S is the standard abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels

explanation.surface: A political figure placing little coronets on heads.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Put on' tells you the second piece is attached to the first; the capital T on Trump is there to make you think of the politician.
explanation.definitionFit: The crown of a hill or head is its summit, so crowns as a plural noun are the uppermost parts.

clue.text: Model poses for Harvard’s third employee there?

indicators.note: to model is to shape or mould material, so these letters are reshaped into a new form
an ordinal number points to a single letter at that position in the following word

blocks.note: taken as written, ready to be remodelled
the letter in third position of the university's name

explanation.surface: A fashion model doing a photo shoot for the university's magazine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'There' points back to Harvard, so the definition depends on the place named in the wordplay: an academic who works at the university.
explanation.definitionFit: A senior university teacher is employed by an institution such as Harvard, so the clue's 'there' makes the job title fit.

clue.text: Close to a fight

blocks.note: taken as written
a single round of boxing or wrestling contest

explanation.surface: Something on the verge of turning into a brawl.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads 'close to a fight' as one phrase; split it after 'to' and the first two words are the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: As a preposition meaning approximately or near, as in 'about ten o'clock', it matches 'close to'.

clue.text: Fashion designer pens new guide

indicators.note: to pen something is to shut it in an enclosure, so one piece encloses another

blocks.note: Coco Chanel, the French couturier
N is the abbreviation for new

explanation.surface: A couturier writing a fresh style handbook.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pens' looks like writing, but here it means encloses: the designer's name holds the single letter.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb, to channel energy or water is to direct it along a course, which is to guide it.

clue.text: Steal golfer’s coins in America

blocks.note: nick is British slang for steal
Ernie Els is a South African major-winning golfer

explanation.surface: Pickpocketing a golf professional's loose change while on tour in the US.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain 'to nick' is everyday slang for to steal. Els is the crossword's favourite golfer because his short name is so useful.
explanation.definitionFit: A US five-cent piece is called by the name of the metal it was made from, so these are American coins.

clue.text: Musical ensemble repelled by ordinary place in Norway

indicators.note: something repelled is driven back, so its letters go backwards

blocks.note: the London Symphony Orchestra
O is a standard abbreviation for ordinary

explanation.surface: An orchestra rebuffed by an unremarkable venue in Scandinavia.
explanation.walkthrough: The ensemble is a specific orchestra known by its initials, the LSO; 'by' here means next to.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the capital city of the Scandinavian kingdom, so a location in that country.

clue.text: Something chemist might give you after beginning of stomach upset

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its opening letter, so only that one is kept

blocks.note: opening letter of the word
a pharmacist dispenses tablets

explanation.surface: A pharmacist handing over medicine for an upset stomach.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stomach upset' looks like one ailment, but 'upset' is the definition at the end; 'after' puts the tablet behind the single letter.
explanation.definitionFit: An upset can be a tumble or knocking over, and a spill is exactly that kind of fall or overturning.

clue.text: Sorting out Iran’s going badly

indicators.note: something done badly is botched and out of order, so these letters come out jumbled

blocks.note: the country's name with its possessive S, plus the following word, taken as written

explanation.surface: A news report on a Middle Eastern country's attempts at reform going wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe-s is part of the fodder: its S is needed to make the ten letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To sort something out is to put it in order, arranging it methodically, so the two phrases are synonyms.

clue.text: Border force operating after Republican row

indicators.note: coming after something means being placed behind it in the sequence

blocks.note: F is the physics symbol for force
R is the abbreviation for a Republican
a machine that is operating is switched on
a tier is a row of seats, one above another

explanation.surface: Immigration officials going into action after a dispute with a US party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Border force' reads as the UK immigration agency, but 'Border' alone is the definition. 'Row' is the line of seats, not a quarrel.
explanation.definitionFit: A frontier is the line or region separating two countries, the same thing as a national boundary.

clue.text: Papa illegally obtained old picture

blocks.note: Papa is P in the NATO phonetic alphabet
hot is slang for stolen goods
O is the abbreviation for old

explanation.surface: Father got hold of a vintage snapshot by dubious means.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old picture' looks like one item, but 'old' belongs to the wordplay and only 'picture' defines.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the short everyday word for a photograph, a picture taken with a camera.

clue.text: Giving cook organic cod with nothing removed

indicators.note: to cook is to fiddle or falsify, so the letters get doctored into a new order
what is removed is taken away, so a letter is struck out

blocks.note: taken as written
zero, nothing, looks like the letter O; this one is taken out

explanation.surface: Handing a chef some organically farmed fish with nothing taken off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cook' looks like the person being given the fish, but it is the anagram signal. One of the two Os in the fodder is dropped before rearranging.
explanation.definitionFit: To accord is to grant or bestow, as in according someone respect, so the participle matches handing over.

clue.text: Judgement broadcast in French church

blocks.note: a signal broadcast has been sent out
the French word for in
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A legal verdict being transmitted from a cathedral in France.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' is not a container signal here: 'in French' gives the French word for in.
explanation.definitionFit: A court's judgement includes the punishment it hands down, which is the sentence passed on the convicted.

clue.text: Fibrous material that’s produced shiny long trousers

indicators.note: to trouser is to pocket something, so the letters sit tucked away inside the phrase

blocks.note: the letters run on across the gap between the two words

explanation.surface: Describing a synthetic fabric that makes glossy full-length slacks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trousers' reads as a noun, the garment, but it is the verb meaning pockets, holding the answer inside 'shiny long'.
explanation.definitionFit: A synthetic polymer spun into threads for textiles, it is a material made of fibres.

clue.text: Stressed European politician has promised 50 per cent off

indicators.note: taking half away removes the first portion of the word

blocks.note: E is the abbreviation for European
a Member of Parliament
taken as written
the back four of its eight letters

explanation.surface: An anxious Euro MP pledging a half-price discount.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stressed' suggests anxiety, but it is the past tense of stressing a point. Half of 'promised' is lopped from the front.
explanation.definitionFit: To stress a word or idea is to give it special weight, a direct synonym in the past tense.

clue.text: Musk is calm with all closures abandoned in Chicago?

indicators.note: a closure is an ending, and abandoning every one drops the final letter of each word

blocks.note: without its final letter
without its final letter
without its final letter

explanation.surface: A billionaire keeping his cool while businesses shut down in an American city.
explanation.walkthrough: Chicago looks like the city, but the question mark warns it is an example: the Kander and Ebb stage show.
explanation.definitionFit: The Broadway show about jazz-age murderesses is a stage production with songs, an example of the genre.

clue.text: Animal found guarding historic city

indicators.note: a guard stands around what it protects, so one piece surrounds another

blocks.note: to found an institution is to create it
the ancient Sumerian city in Mesopotamia

explanation.surface: A beast discovered standing sentry over an ancient town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Found' reads as the past of find but is the verb to found, establish. Ur is the crossword's standby ancient city.
explanation.definitionFit: Any living being, especially a beast rather than a plant, is called a creature, a general synonym.

clue.text: Trouble for no female in ship’s crew

indicators.note: having no woman means the letter standing for female is struck out
being inside something means being enclosed by it

blocks.note: SS is a steamship, the prefix on ship names
to ail is to trouble or afflict
the word with its F, for female, removed

explanation.surface: Bad luck for any woman aboard, in old seafaring superstition.
explanation.walkthrough: F is the abbreviation for female, so 'for' with no female leaves OR. The steamship letters split around the middle.
explanation.definitionFit: A ship's crew is made up of seamen, so the plural noun names the people who work the vessel.

clue.text: Group of players generating the roars outside clubs

indicators.note: generating means producing something new, so the letters are made into a fresh arrangement
one thing outside another wraps around it

blocks.note: taken as written
C is the abbreviation for the card suit

explanation.surface: A sports team whose play draws cheers from the crowd at golf or football clubs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Players' suggests sport, but these play instruments.
explanation.definitionFit: A large ensemble of musicians playing together is literally a band of instrumental players.

clue.text: Almost injure head getting tackle on horse?

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the final letter is dropped

blocks.note: harm, to injure, without its last letter
a ness is a headland, as in Loch Ness or Dungeness

explanation.surface: A rugby or football tackle that nearly hurts someone's head, oddly involving a horse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tackle' is not a sporting challenge but gear, as in fishing tackle; 'head' is a promontory.
explanation.definitionFit: Straps and fittings by which a horse is attached to a cart are its gear, so tack or tackle.

clue.text: Chauffeur perhaps specified collecting right vehicle

indicators.note: to collect something is to gather it in, so one piece takes the other inside

blocks.note: a set time is one specified
R is the abbreviation for right
a van is a vehicle

explanation.surface: A driver who was told to pick up the correct car.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Perhaps' marks the chauffeur as one example of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A chauffeur is a domestic employee who drives, an example of someone employed to wait on a household.

clue.text: Description of Cleopatra? Fair, devious, cold and short

indicators.note: devious means winding or crooked, so these letters wander from their order
something short is cut down, so the last letter goes

blocks.note: taken as written, ready to be twisted
C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps
with its final letter cut

explanation.surface: A character sketch of the Egyptian queen: beautiful, scheming, aloof and brusque.
explanation.walkthrough: The list of adjectives seems to describe Cleopatra, but they are wordplay. Egypt is in Africa, so the definition fits her geographically.
explanation.definitionFit: Cleopatra ruled Egypt, a country on that continent, so she could be described by its adjective.

clue.text: Very old social worker keeping inactive on a regular basis

indicators.note: regularly means at even intervals, so every other letter is kept
to keep something is to hold it within, so one piece goes inside another

blocks.note: the ant is the classic social insect, a worker in its colony
the second, fourth, sixth and eighth letters

explanation.surface: An elderly welfare officer who keeps up their idleness routinely.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Social worker' reads as a job title, but crosswords use it for an insect that lives in colonies.
explanation.definitionFit: Something extremely aged or dating from the distant past is described with this adjective, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Little container in street

indicators.note: being inside something means one piece is enclosed by another

blocks.note: a can is a tin container
ST is the abbreviation for street

explanation.surface: A small bin left out on the road.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Little container' reads as one phrase, but 'Little' is the definition, an adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: As an adjective meaning barely sufficient, as in scant attention, it matches 'little' in amount.

clue.text: American advantage once more

blocks.note: A is the abbreviation for American
a benefit or profit you come out ahead with

explanation.surface: The United States gaining the upper hand yet another time.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the two words at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: An adverb meaning another time or a further occasion, interchangeable with the phrase in a sentence.

clue.text: Put down ‘er instrument

blocks.note: to put something down in writing is to record it
the dropped-aitch form, taken as written

explanation.surface: A cockney telling someone to set down her musical instrument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Put down' could mean belittle or set down, but here it means note in writing.
explanation.definitionFit: A simple wooden or plastic woodwind pipe played in schools is this type of musical instrument.

clue.text: Young lover’s little jumper enthralling this writer

indicators.note: to enthral is to hold captive, so one piece is held within another

blocks.note: roo is short for kangaroo, a hopping animal
the setter referring to themselves

explanation.surface: A boy's small sweater charming the author.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain a jumper is a sweater, which is the misleading sense here; the jumper is an animal that leaps.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare's teenage hero is the archetypal youthful romantic, and his name is used for any ardent lover.

clue.text: Waste time dropping off daughter’s friend

indicators.note: dropping something off means letting it go, so a letter is removed

blocks.note: to dally is to dawdle
D is the abbreviation for daughter; this letter is removed

explanation.surface: Dawdling while giving a lift home to a child's playmate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dropping off daughter' paints the school run, but it means removing the letter D from the front.
explanation.definitionFit: A supporter or partner who is on your side is a friend in the broad sense, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Actress and I tangled crossing a set of steps

indicators.note: tangled things are twisted and muddled, so these letters are mixed up
to cross something can mean to straddle it, so one piece spans the other

blocks.note: the two words taken as written, 'and' joining them
taken as written

explanation.surface: A performer and the speaker got in a muddle going over some stairs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Actress' wants a synonym like STAR, but it is taken literally as anagram fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: A flight of stairs with its banisters and supporting structure is a series of steps joining floors.

clue.text: Where drivers might stop, somewhat unable to move backwards

indicators.note: somewhat means to some extent, so only part of the phrase is used
going backwards means reading the letters from the other end

blocks.note: the letters spanning the end of the first word and start of the last

explanation.surface: A broken-down car that cannot go into reverse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unable to move backwards' reads like a gearbox fault, but 'backwards' reverses the hidden letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A roadside lodging for motorists, it is somewhere drivers might break a journey overnight.

clue.text: Concluded poet lacks heart

indicators.note: the heart of a word is its central letter, and lacking it means that letter goes

blocks.note: John Donne, the metaphysical poet

explanation.surface: A judgement that a versifier has no soul.
explanation.walkthrough: The five-letter poet loses his middle N.
explanation.definitionFit: When something has concluded it is finished or completed, so the past participles are synonyms.

clue.text: Still paper’s delivered

indicators.note: a speech is delivered when it is spoken, so we want how a word is heard

blocks.note: writing paper and envelopes collectively, spelt with an E

explanation.surface: A newsagent remarking that the newspaper has arrived.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Delivered' suggests a paper round, but it means spoken. The two words differ only in an A or an E: the A spelling means not moving.
explanation.definitionFit: Something motionless is still, so the adjective spelt with A is a direct synonym.
